title: OpenBikeComputer map catalog (schema_version 2)
description: The schema_version 2 map catalog: one schema, a set of skins, named cell-set regions with drawable boundaries, and digest-pinned per-band cell indices. A consumer prices a selection from this document alone — total bytes and bytes per band, which is the per-file projection a volume set needs — and verifies each satellite against the `bytes` + `sha256` pinned here. The satellite documents are `$defs/CellIndexDocument` and `$defs/RegionCellsDocument`. Normative contract: OBCC_Spec.md §11, with OBCA_Spec.md for the grid, bands, and assembly.

schema_version.description: Envelope version, `2`. Checked before any other field.

generated_at.description: When this root was generated, RFC 3339 UTC — the only wall clock on the generation path (`OBCC_Spec.md` §5).

schema.description: The catalog's **single** schema. Not an array: the hosted store carries the 7-LOD bikepacking ladder and nothing else, because a second schema would make the whole planet-shaped cell store exist twice (§11.2, epic #1016 D2).

skins.description: Every skin offered, sorted by `id`. Inlined rather than referenced: one is ≈ 2 KB and a builder needs all of them at once to draw a picker.

cell_index.description: One entry per band, sorted by `cell_log2` descending (§11.6).

artifacts.description: Legacy whole-region artifacts during migration (§11.9), with exactly v1 §3 semantics. A v2 consumer MAY ignore it; a finished migration omits it. This generator never emits it — a v2 tree has no whole-region artifacts to describe — but the field is here because a consumer built on these types must be able to read a bakery that is still serving both.

SchemaEntry.description: The schema: the identity of the cell store. Everything a consumer needs to price a selection and an assembler needs to stamp a skin, with no out-of-band constant (§11.3).

revision.description: Monotone content revision. Every cell states the revision it was baked at, and a bump invalidates the whole store — assembly copies chunk bytes between files, which is only meaningful within one revision (`OBCA_Spec.md` §6.3).

obcm_version.description: OBCM format version, read from the **cells' own headers**; every cell agrees or generation fails (§11.9).

grid.description: The grid's constants, restated so no consumer hard-codes them.

bands.description: The band table: which LODs and which non-geometry sections live in which cell size, and which file of a volume set they assemble into.

styles.description: The canonical style-id assignment. `obc-pack` numbers feature types 1-based in config document order and every feature header in every chunk references those ids, so the assignment is part of the cells' bytes — schema data, never skin data (§11.3).

routing.description: Routing facts baked into the cells. The island-prune threshold is schema data: two cells pruned at different thresholds do not assemble into a graph with consistent semantics (`OBCA_Spec.md` §3.5).

chunk_size.description: The per-LOD chunk capacity bound the cells were written with (`OBCM_Spec.md` §3). An assembler re-checks every copied offset pair against it.

GridEntry.description: `OBCA_Spec.md` §1.1's constants. Published so a consumer computing a cell's square or an assembly bbox never hard-codes a power of two.

LodEntry.description: One rung of the LOD ladder.

max_mpp.description: Meters-per-pixel upper bound; `null` for the `+inf` coarsest level (`OBCM_Spec.md` §3).

band.description: The band whose cells carry this LOD.

BandEntry.description: One band: a cell size plus the content its cells carry.

id.description: Stable band id, e.g. `fine`. Also the band's segment in a cell URL.

lods.description: Ladder LODs this band's cells carry, ascending. Empty for the `core` band.

sections.description: Non-geometry sections this band's cells carry. Only the `core` band has any.

role.description: Which file of a volume set this band becomes.

BandSection.description: A non-geometry OBCM section a band may carry.

BandRole.description: Which file of a volume set a band's content assembles into (`OBCA_Spec.md` §5.1).

oneOf.description: The one unsplittable file: nav graph, POIs, style table. Carries no LOD, because its headroom under `4 GiB − 1` is the design's hard limit.
The single whole-assembly coarse shard that keeps a zoomed-out viewport a one-file read.
An ordinary geometry shard's content; splits by bbox as needed.

StyleAssignment.description: One feature type's canonical style id — the assignment baked into every chunk.

id.description: 1-based style id, as referenced by feature headers (`OBCM_Spec.md` §2, §5.2).

RoutingEntry.description: The routing facts a cell's nav bytes were produced under.

min_component_edges.description: Island-prune threshold, applied at **assembly** over the merged graph (`OBCA_Spec.md` §3.5/§4.6) — a cell bake prunes only strictly interior components.

SkinEntry.description: A skin: the presentation half of what v1 called a preset. Stamped onto ~2 KB of an assembly at assembly time, so it is baked into nothing and invalidates nothing (§11.4).

version.description: The skin's content version. Unlike v1's `preset_version` there is no per-artifact counterpart, because no artifact carries a skin.

styles.description: One entry per `schema.styles` feature type, in schema id order. A skin that misses one would ship a map with an invisible layer; one that names a feature type the schema lacks is stale (§11.4).

preview.description: Rendered preview asset, resolved like a `url`. Absent until one exists.

SkinStyle.description: One feature type's presentation values — the seven bytes of a style record a skin owns. The **id** is not here: it belongs to the schema, and a skin may not renumber it (`OBCA_Spec.md` §4.7).

color2.description: Optional RGB565 secondary color; `null` when the style has none.

RegionEntry.description: A named region: a boundary to draw and a cell set to fetch (§11.5).

id.description: Slash-separated id, same grammar as v1's `region_id`.

parent.description: The enclosing region's id, when the curation nests.

boundary.description: Simplified outline for drawing (§11.8). Presentation only.

bytes.description: Total bytes of every cell in this region's set, across all bands.

bytes_by_band.description: Those bytes per band, summing to `bytes`. This is what makes the §5.7 pre-download projection *per file* rather than merely per set: a volume set's roles partition by band, so the `core` band's bytes are the core file's bytes.

partial_cell_count.description: How many of those cells are `partial` (§11.6). `0` for fully covered curation.

cells_url.description: Where the region's cell-id list lives (§11.7).

cells_bytes.description: Size of that document, in bytes.

cells_sha256.description: Its digest — the pin that keeps the satellite all-or-nothing.

Boundary.description: A region's simplified outline, in integer microdegrees, `[lat, lon]` per point. Presentation only: it MUST NOT be used to compute a cell set (that is stored, §11.7), to price a selection, or as a packer input bbox. The coverage outline a builder draws for a live selection is a different object — the union of the selected cells' squares, computed client-side — and is deliberately not in the catalog.

tolerance_udeg.description: The tolerance the outline was reduced at.

rings.description: One or more closed rings; the first is an exterior and any ring nested in it is a hole. A region that is several disjoint pieces repeats that pattern.

CellIndexRef.description: The root's pin on one band's cell index (§11.6).

sha256.description: Its digest. A satellite that does not match MUST be rejected and the root kept.

ArtifactEntry.description: One published `.obcm` artifact: a (region, preset) pair.

region_id.description: Slash-separated region id mirroring the Geofabrik hierarchy, e.g. `europe/switzerland`. Derived from the artifact's directory path.

preset_id.description: The preset this artifact was built with; matches a `presets[].id`.

preset_version.description: The preset's `version` **as recorded by the bake job that produced this artifact** — read from its sidecar, not from the preset config sitting in the tree when the manifest was generated. That distinction is the whole point of the field. A preset restyle invalidates only that preset's artifacts, so partial re-bakes are the normal operation (a full bake is ~20 CPU-hours). Copied from the current preset config it would equal `presets[].version` by construction and could never signal anything, while every not-yet-re-baked artifact silently claimed styling it does not have. Lower than the matching `presets[].version` means exactly one thing: this artifact carries older styling (`OBCC_Spec.md` §3).

obcm_version.description: OBCM format version, read from the artifact's own header — never from the builder's intent. A consumer MUST refuse an artifact whose version the target firmware cannot read (`OBCC_Spec.md` §6).

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the artifact bytes.

bbox.description: Coverage bbox, copied from the artifact header. Descriptive output, never a build input — see [`CoverageBBox`].

built_at.description: When the artifact was packed, RFC 3339 UTC.

source_snapshot.description: Date of the OSM extract it was packed from, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

url.description: Absolute or root-relative URL the artifact can be fetched from.

CoverageBBox.description: The artifact's coverage bounding box in **microdegrees**, exactly as the OBCM header stores it. This is what the packed file actually covers, which is always a little wider than the extract box it was cut from: complete ways and stray coastline features push it out. `obc-sim/assets/repack.sh` therefore forbids feeding a header bbox back in as an extract bbox — self-sourcing ratchets the box wider on every re-pack (a fixture once grew to 14.5 MB that way). That rule is about *inputs*. This field is an *output*: the honest answer to "what does this download cover?", which is the only question a catalog consumer asks. It MUST NOT be used as a packer input bbox, and `OBCC_Spec.md` §4 says so normatively. Microdegrees rather than degrees, because the format's own unit is integer microdegrees and integers serialize deterministically; floats would not.

CellEntry.description: One published cell. There is deliberately no bbox: a cell's coverage is exactly its grid square, which the `id` determines to the microdegree (OBCA_Spec.md §1.3), and the generator verifies the artifact's own OBCM header bbox against it at bake time. A stored copy could only agree (redundant) or disagree (a lie).

built_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC, recorded by the bake job.

sources.description: Every source extract this cell was baked from, sorted by `extract_id`.

partial.description: `true` iff those sources do not fully cover the cell's square (`OBCA_Spec.md` §3.7). A consumer MUST NOT present a partial cell as canonical coverage.

CellSource.description: One source extract behind a cell.

schema_revision.description: The revision every cell in this document was baked at.

CellIndexDocument.description: A band's cell index: the satellite the root pins (§11.6).

RegionCellsDocument.description: A region's cell list: the satellite `RegionEntry::cells_url` points at (§11.7). Cell ids only — every other fact is in the band's index, keyed by the same id.

not.description: §11.9: `presets` MUST NOT appear in a v2 root.
